_purpose: Catalogue-shaped rows for the six tables present in BBW but absent from docs/data-model/object-catalog.md. Directly insertable; not raw field dumps.
_CAVEAT_fieldCountsAreGlobalOnly: fieldCount here is the GLOBAL field count. The source sweep passed showGlobal=true. These counts may rise after the showGlobal=false re-sweep, and ChangeManage/VirtualTemplateMember at 1 field each are the likeliest to grow. Do not publish these counts as final.

_columnMethodology.outDegree: COMPUTED AND VALIDATED. Rule: count fields whose type string ends in 'ID' and does NOT start with 'Dropdown (' - i.e. typed FKs to business objects, excluding code-table dropdowns. Validated against 12 objects the catalogue already scores (Allowance, AssetHistory, AuditTable, EntityTemplate, TaskPredecessor, AccrualTransaction, AlternateRentSchedule, AllowanceTransaction, Asset, BudgetLineItem, VirtualTemplateSchedule, VirtualTemplateFolder), spanning 1 to 122 fields: 12/12 exact match. A first attempt that included Dropdown types scored 5/12 and was discarded.
_columnMethodology.inDegree: NOT SUPPLIED. The same approach scored only 4/9 against catalogue controls and under-counted badly (Asset 0 vs 13, TaskGroup 0 vs 11, BudgetTemplate 0 vs 14). The FK type vocabulary does not consistently name its target object, and the global-only capture is probably missing FK columns. Left null rather than published wrong - compute it from the existing FK graph in docs/mindmap/, which already has the edges.
_columnMethodology.physicalTable: NOT OBSERVED. ShowObjectDetails.jsp gives the CamelCase object name, never the PG table name; the catalogue's Table(s) column comes from _lucernex_objects_summary.txt, which does not cover these six. physicalTable_conventional is a mechanical CamelCase-to-snake_case guess and MUST be verified before use.
_columnMethodology.spine: Applied mechanically per the catalogue's own definition - entity_scoped if the object carries a ProjectEntityID FK, firm_global otherwise.

_notableFinding: The three PunchList child tables reference their parent through a column typed 'Text' (PunchListID / PunchListTaskID), not a typed object FK. Any FK-graph built by matching type strings will therefore show the Punch List family as four disconnected tables with no parent-child edges. That is a graph artefact, not the real shape.

The Virtual*Template read-only projection for member/committee templates, sibling to VirtualTemplateBudget, VirtualTemplateFolder and VirtualTemplateSchedule — but exposing only ProjectEntityID at the global layer, unlike those three which carry 16-17 fields.
A snagging/defect list raised against an entity — named list with status, due date, assignees, and a running completed-vs-total task count.
rows.purposeEvidence: Derived from the observed field list
rows.outOfScopeReason: Construction snagging. Zero coverage across all 38 approved BRDs (punch/snag/defect list/site survey all return zero files, grep verified against a control term). Two BRDs place construction management in the legacy ASG Edge product, which ASG Edge+ integrates with and migrates away from - so this is explicitly another product's scope, not merely unrequested. Corroborated independently by the field list itself - see _twoIndependentLinesOfEvidence.

_twoIndependentLinesOfEvidence: The out-of-scope call on the Punch List family rests on TWO independent lines of evidence that agree: (1) zero coverage across all 38 approved BRDs, with two BRDs placing construction management in the legacy ASG Edge product; and (2) the field list alone - PunchListTask carries LatitudeDegrees, LongitudeDegrees, HasLocationCoordinates and DocumentIDList, i.e. geotagged defect items with photo attachments, which is mobile field inspection. Neither argument depends on the other.
